summary: Describes how DHCP and BOOTP clients and servers interact, since DHCP does everything BOOTP does and more.

eli5.summary: Old and new machines of the same kind sometimes meet. This memo says how they should behave so both can be happy.

questions: can a dhcp server answer bootp clients
can a dhcp server serve bootp clients
how does dhcp work with bootp
subtitle: How DHCP servers and clients cope with the older BOOTP protocol they grew out of.

tldr.problem: DHCP messages are based on BOOTP messages, so DHCP and BOOTP participants can meet on the same network and need agreed rules for talking to each other.
tldr.mechanism: A DHCP server tells the two kinds of client apart by the 'DHCP message type' option and may answer BOOTP clients with plain BOOTREPLY messages. A DHCP client may accept a BOOTP server's reply, treating the address as having an infinite lease.
tldr.outcome: Supporting BOOTP clients is optional for servers, and handing them automatic addresses must be a switch that defaults to off.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 1534 as a Draft Standard and shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it. It builds on RFC 1531, RFC 1532 and RFC 1533.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) delivers configuration parameters to hosts using TCP/IP. Its message format is based on BOOTP, so in some circumstances DHCP and BOOTP participants can exchange messages. This document specifies how they interoperate.

DHCP also changes a term: the BOOTP 'vendor extensions' field is now the 'options' field, and the tagged items inside it are simply 'options'. A message carrying a 'DHCP message type' option is named by its type, so type 1 is a DHCPDISCOVER.
sections.eli5: The new system was built from the old one, so they can talk. This note says how.

sections.title: BOOTP Clients and DHCP Servers
sections.content:
A DHCP server treats any message with a 'DHCP message type' option (option 51) as coming from a DHCP client, and any without it as coming from a BOOTP client. Supporting BOOTP clients is optional, at the administrator's discretion. A server that is not configured to support them silently discards a BOOTREQUEST.

A server that does support them may supply static addresses, previously assigned by an administrator, or automatic addresses picked from its pool, or both. Because BOOTP clients may not be ready for automatic addresses, the feature must be configurable and must default off. Since a BOOTP client knows nothing of leases, the server must assign an infinite lease, and such addresses cannot be automatically reassigned.

The server MUST behave according to the BOOTP protocol. It MUST send a BOOTREPLY rather than a DHCPOFFER, MUST NOT include the 'DHCP message type' option, and MUST NOT exceed the BOOTREPLY size limit. It marks the binding BOUND after sending, since the client will not send a DHCPREQUEST or expect a DHCPACK. It MAY send DHCP options to a BOOTP client.
sections.eli5: If a letter has the new-style stamp, the server treats it as new-style. Otherwise it answers in the old style, and it is careful before giving old-style users a permanent address.

sections.title: DHCP Clients and BOOTP Servers
sections.content:
A DHCP client MAY use a reply from a BOOTP server if the configuration it returns is acceptable. It MUST assume that an IP address from a BOOTP server has an infinite lease. It SHOULD prefer a reply from a DHCP server over one from a BOOTP server.

The memo says security issues are not discussed in it.
sections.eli5: A new-style computer can accept an answer from an old-style server, but it prefers a new-style one and assumes the address is its to keep.
